what: Jeff Rubenstein's verdicts on the 8 passages of the 2026-11-12 email: the 6 non-yes of Simon's pre-read of the 60-story Shas precision sample, plus 2 stories the site lacks.
cover_note: The interface did not work for me

verdicts.his_words: Not a story. The narrative elements appear within the give and take of the legal discussion to work out the law. They are hypothetical or possible answers, not events.
Not a story. Similar to the last case. This is the Talmud discussing a story that appeared previously and trying to make sense of it. But it is a legal discussion.
Borderline. Agreed. There are two events the dialogue is not really connected to the events. So a borderline case.

Borderline. There is some change, the hen lives, but there is hardly drama or development or real change. Some would count it a minimal story: you have a protagonist, two events (the splinting, the hen living) and change. If the choice were story or not, I would say story. But if we have the option for borderline story, I think it is borderline
Borderline. I agree with your classification. The return of the practice could be a literary ruling, not a real event. Even if it is, there is not much drama or development.
Not a story. This is a legal ruling, a question and answer. It start with the setting, that Ulla visited Asi bar Hini. But that is not enough for a story.
Not a story for our database. This is a story based on the biblical events, an exegetical narrative. We are collecting sage-stories of post biblical times.
verdicts.note: the two lepers Et and Hev ("Vahev in Sufa"); starts at the bottom of 54a, the site has only the 54b part (berakhot-54b-0-0, a sample story Simon graded yes). End segment not stated by him

verdicts.his_words: Story. But this story basically appears in the Mishnah (Sanhedrin 7:2) in slightly different form. Here it is indeed presented as a baraita. I think it could be included. (The Talmud follows by saying it was a separate incident (than the Mishnah) but scholars would consider them two versions of one source. In any case, I would include it.
verdicts.note: v14 run 1 found it at LOW_CONFIDENCE, so the definite-only site filter held it back

sample_precision.evidence: MIXED: 7 of the 60 carry Jeff's verdict (measured: the 6 non-yes he was sent, and Berakhot 54b:0, covered by his ruling on the lepers passage); the other 53 are Simon's pre-read yes (the project owner, indicated), never shown to Jeff. So the not-a-story count is a measured lower bound, and the story count an indicated upper bound.
